pr_title: Fix CCR following a datastream with closed indices on the follower corrupting the datastream
pr_body:
Reproducer and fix for #87048.

Reproduces the edge case by closing follower index that is part of a datastream and then recreating and re-adding that same
index on the leader to make it get picked up by the auto-follower again. Using stats call in the test mainly to reproduce
the exact issue that motivated #87048 and to show that the datastream is correctly resolved by the index name expression resolver.

closes #87048

issue_context.title: CCR AutoFollowCoordinator can trigger put-follow actions that can corrupt datastreams in an edge case
comments: retracting this for now ... there's an error in the reasoning here.
This issue description doesn't mention any Elasticsearch version(s).  I guess we know at least 1 version that has this problem.  Is it a regression and should get that label?

review_comments: Can we also assert that the index is now part of the data stream on the follower and is opened?

So in this case, the new index being followed is not added to the data stream, but is being replicated by ccr? And the original, but closed backing index remains to exist and data stream remains to refer to the closed backing index?

The "new" index is already part of the data stream, we merely reopened it due to the restore action => must not add it again.


->
 
> And the original, but closed backing index remains to exist and data stream remains to refer to the closed backing index?

no its' reopened like with a normal snapshot restore :)

I would find it more explicit to use the `currentState` above to detect that the index already existed and thus should not be added to the data stream? (and perhaps rename `currentState` to `previousState` for readability).

We should then assert that it already exists there. And here we can assert that it cannot exist already (or rely on the new assertion in the `DataStream` constructor).

I'd rather not use the `currentState` here to be honest. It will work now, but we go through super complicated code when restoring the datastream in the restore service, I find it much easier to reason about taking the information from the builder.
If I use the `currentState` then the whole logic becomes predicated on a bunch of assumptions (like that we won't ever remove an index in the restore action) and as a result (at least to me) much less obviously correct.

I'd hope we can find a better way to signal this then, perhaps expand the updater contract to include this boolean information. I am OK with merging as is, but would like to see this in a follow-up.

The current way seems to be somewhat lenient and could "repair" something inadvertently.
